physical_mismatch.note: strong_queue_match_coverage_pct (0.5%) is NOT a deliverability rate. The ISO interconnection queues ARE fully ingested (16253 records {'caiso': 170, 'nyiso': 2195, 'miso': 69, 'spp': 960, 'pjm': 9263, 'ercot': 1845, 'iso': 1751}), but they are GENERATION-side supply queues: only 26 of 16253 records are data-center-load related (9 strong-matched to tracker projects). Data-center LOADS largely interconnect through a separate load-study process not in these generation queues, so queue-matching under-counts data-center deliverability by construction. Deliverability is therefore read from the tracker's construction-status (non-primary): most announced AI/data-center MW is not yet built or permitted (high announced_only + permit_not_confirmed) -- a directional stranding/timeline signal. A true firm-vs-queue rate needs utility large-load / load-interconnection data, not generation queues.

gpu_economics_mismatch.accounting_vs_modeled_life_note: Positive gap = accounting useful life longer than observed secondary market / rental rate compression implies. Classic bubble signal per Burry-style depreciation reality check.

source_backed_gap.book_life_primary_anchor: Amazon revised server+networking useful life 6yr -> 5yr eff. Jan 1 2025; ~$0.7B reduction to 2025 operating income (+$0.6B early-retirement)
source_backed_gap.gap_summary: Deployed AI GPUs (H100/A100/H800-class) lost ~65.5% of their on-demand RENTAL yield within ~18-24 months -- the economic monetization curve -- while the same assets are booked straight-line over 5-7 years. Amazon's own SEC filing already revised server/networking life 6yr -> 5yr citing AI obsolescence pace. So the book life materially overstates the economic life of the first revenue-generating window, understating depreciation (and overstating current earnings / secured-collateral value).
counter_signals: Newest generation still appreciating (NVIDIA B200 / GB200) -- the gap is a DEPLOYED-fleet signal, not a new-silicon one.
A 2026 rental rebound (HBM/DRAM shortage) lifted some contract rates ~40%.
Used-unit RESALE prices held 75-85% of cost through ~24 months in a supply-tight market; the gap is clearest on the rental-yield axis, more nuanced on resale.
source_backed_gap.source_tiers: rental/secondary = reputable market trackers; book-life revision = SEC 10-Q (primary).

cluster_interest_coverage.note: Cluster coverage = sum(EBITDA-or-operating-income) / sum(annual interest expense) across source-backed issuers. Coverage < 1 means operations do not cover interest alone (before any principal). Loss-making issuers carry negative EBITDA, so the ratio is negative. Realistic-utilization stress is forward-looking and applied separately; these figures are as-reported.

scenario_stress.note: Cluster cash-flow stress: base financials are primary-sourced (11-issuer fixture); the stress PARAMETERS (utilization miss, rate shock, GPU-life compression) are labeled assumptions. EBITDA falls ~1:1 with the revenue lost to a utilization miss (high fixed cost), interest reprices at refinancing by shock/avg-rate (~8%). 'Breaching' = stressed interest coverage < 1 or negative EBITDA. A MAJORITY of issuers already breach at the BASE scenario (which applies ZERO shock), so the financed core is already fragile before any shock -- the aggregate ~1.35x coverage is a CoreWeave/CleanSpark concentration artifact masking the loss-makers; the adverse/severe scenarios only deepen the breach.

gds_graph_analytics.chokepoint_read: Structural chokepoints (betweenness): the AI-infra subgraph's top node is AMAZON ENERGY LLC, and 4/6 of its top chokepoints are POWER/ENERGY procurement intermediaries (Amazon Energy, Microsoft Energy, Shell Energy). The full graph agrees (Shell Energy North America (US), L.P.). The entities sitting on the most exposure-propagation paths are the power buyers/sellers -- the 'power is the binding constraint' thesis confirmed from graph TOPOLOGY, independent of the interconnection-queue/physical layer.
gds_graph_analytics.systemic_importance_read: Notional-weighted PageRank puts the big banks (JPMorgan, Bank of America) at the top of the full graph and Equinix + the financing agents (Goldman, Wilmington Trust, Morgan Stanley) at the top of the AI subgraph -- the most systemically exposed nodes by weighted dollar flow are the lenders and the colocation landlord, not the neoclouds themselves.
gds_graph_analytics.boundedness_read: Louvain modularity is 0.7574 on the AI subgraph (28 communities) and 0.65 on the full graph. CAVEAT: the ai_infra subgraph is SPARSE (216 nodes / 232 edges, avg degree ~2.2), and high modularity on a near-tree graph is partly a sparsity artifact, not strong evidence of cohesive community structure -- so this is at most a WEAK, corroborating hint toward the 'bounded cluster' conclusion, not an independent confirmation. The load-bearing boundedness evidence remains the entity-classification map (~4% distress) and the capture-recapture robustness check, not this modularity number.
gds_graph_analytics.coreweave_nuance: CoreWeave is the FINANCING/demand chokepoint (the demand-failure cascade routes ~$25B through it) but only the rank-5 TOPOLOGICAL chokepoint by betweenness -- the exposure topology is dominated by the energy intermediaries. The two lenses highlight DIFFERENT single-points-of-failure (financing vs power), and both are real.
gds_graph_analytics.note: Neo4j GDS (betweenness, notional-weighted PageRank, Louvain) over the source-backed capital-exposure graph (5,102 nodes / 7,617 edges loaded via MERGE). Real graph theory, not the in-code approximation. Findings: power/energy intermediaries are the structural chokepoints; banks + Equinix carry the systemic weight; high modularity confirms the cluster is topologically bounded. Descriptive structural analysis; does not change the evidence gate.

circular_financing.disclosure_gap: Neither NVIDIA's nor Microsoft's filings name the supplier-AND-investor circularity (NVIDIA) or the Microsoft->OpenAI->CoreWeave->NVIDIA chain as a related-party or customer/supplier-concentration risk; NVIDIA's customer concentration is anonymized (Customer A/B/C). The round-trip is forensic framing, not a filing-disclosed risk -- a disclosure-gap red flag in its own right.
circular_financing.demand_durability_read: NVIDIA is a filing-verified equity investor in 3 of its own GPU-cloud customers (Applied Digital, CoreWeave, Nebius); 2 have a filing-verified return-purchase leg, closing ~$4.0B of reciprocal (supplier-funds-customer) capital. 2 reciprocal loop(s) are filing-verified on every leg CoreWeave -> NVIDIA -> CoreWeave; NVIDIA -> Nebius -> NVIDIA. 4 larger macro loop(s) exist but rest on a press-reported/inferred edge (e.g. the NVIDIA->OpenAI framework commitment), so they are flagged and capped, not relied on. Net: the AI-infra demand signal is partly reciprocal -- the supplier finances the buyers -- so headline take-or-pay backlog overstates independent, arm's-length end-demand.
circular_financing.interpretation_caveat: The equity-investment and GPU-purchase legs are LEGALLY SEPARATE transactions; their co-existence does not prove the identical dollars circulate (Nebius is the one filing that earmarks the supplier's proceeds for the supplier's hardware). The defensible inference is narrower and still material: the dominant supplier is also an equity investor in its own customers, so (a) it is incentivized to sustain their apparent demand and (b) the demand those customers represent is NOT arm's-length -- a vendor-financed buyer is not an independent validator of end-demand. This impairs demand DURABILITY; it is a red flag, not proof of fabricated revenue.
circular_financing.note: Reciprocal/round-trip financing detection via directed money-flow cycle search. Filing-verified loops are primary-source on every leg; loops touching a press-reported or inferred edge are FLAGGED and capped at INFERRED (<=0.45) -- they never drive the verdict. Vendor round-tripping is the Lucent/Nortel late-cycle tell; the finding here is that the structure is present and partly filing-verified, which is itself novel relative to the purely customer-concentration framing.

per_offtaker.basis: Pre-profitability. Microsoft carries OpenAI under the equity method (HLBV) as a 'funding commitment' with revenue-sharing and recognized large OpenAI-related equity-method swings; OpenAI is capitalized by Microsoft ($13B), an NVIDIA letter of intent (up to $100B, NON-BINDING, $0 funded), and SoftBank. Its ~$18.4B multi-year CoreWeave take-or-pay far exceeds its operating cash flow and depends on continued external fundraising -- it cannot be honored from operations. Fragile demand, and circular (its compute vendor's supplier and its largest backer are inside the same loop).

Hyperscaler with large positive operating cash flow; the ~$14.2B commitment is spread through December 2031 (~$2.4B/yr), small vs annual operating cash flow and payable from operations. Durable demand. (Funding-class is a first-principles judgment; no single offtaker-cash-flow figure is cited here.)

demand_funding_durability.durability_read: 56.4% of the cluster's CLASSIFIED named take-or-pay backlog (~$18.4B of $32.6B) rests on capital_markets_dependent offtaker(s) (OpenAI) -- demand that is NOT payable from the offtaker's operations and depends on continued external fundraising. A MAJORITY of the named contracted demand is therefore a bet on open capital markets, not on end-customer operating cash flow -- and (via the circular-financing loop) that offtaker is partly funded by the cluster's own GPU supplier and largest current customer. The hyperscaler slices remain durable; the contracted-backlog 'proof of demand' is bifurcated, and its larger half is the fragile, circular one.
demand_funding_durability.caveat: Dollar commitments are filing-verified; the funding-class is a FIRST-PRINCIPLES judgment (payable-from-operations vs requires-external-capital) backed by the cited filing where one exists. The hyperscaler slices (Microsoft, Meta) are genuinely durable -- the finding is the BIFURCATION of demand, not blanket fragility. SCOPE: the percentage is of the NAMED, classified backlog only (OpenAI + Meta dollar commitments); Microsoft's commitment is sized only as ~67% of CoreWeave revenue (no multi-year dollar figure disclosed) and is durable, so the fragile share of TOTAL contracted demand is LOWER than the named-slice figure -- the precise claim is 'a majority of the NAMED take-or-pay backlog', not of all demand. Capped as a corroborating decomposition; never drives the evidence gate.

fragile_demand_failure_cascade.trigger_basis: Seeded from the capital-markets-dependent offtaker(s) the durability layer flags as most likely to fail. The 'debt_at_risk_usd' is the directly-hit issuer's ENTIRE total debt (e.g. CoreWeave's full ~$25B), NOT apportioned to this offtaker's revenue share -- it is a gross UPPER BOUND on directly-exposed leverage, not a probability-weighted or offtaker-attributable loss. The fragile offtaker is one of several customers (Microsoft is CoreWeave's largest at ~67%), so its withdrawal alone would impair, not necessarily zero, the issuer; read this as 'the leverage sitting on the issuer the fragile demand touches', a contagion-surface measure.

demand_side_funding.bear_case_read: mixed_and_weakening: aggregate operating cash flow still covers AI cash capex (1.76x) and the largest players (Microsoft/Meta) self-fund, BUT the demand side is NOT uniformly cash-funded -- 2 player(s) are predominantly debt-funded (e.g. Oracle, capex > OCF), others use mixed debt, and the mega-caps carry large OFF-BALANCE-SHEET datacenter lease pipelines NOT in this ratio. So the bear/rational-growth case holds for the cash-rich core of the demand side today, but leverage is rising at the margin and via off-BS leases -- the demand side is not an unconditional backstop for the financed core.
demand_side_funding.note: Demand-side (hyperscaler/offtaker) economics. cash_coverage_of_capex = aggregate operating cash flow / aggregate AI(-or-total) capex; >1 means the demand side self-funds its CASH capex. CAVEAT (key hidden leverage): this ratio is on the income/cash-flow statement only -- it excludes the large and fast-growing OFF-BALANCE-SHEET datacenter financing (finance leases + not-yet-commenced build-to-suit leases, e.g. Microsoft's ~$196.6B of not-yet-commenced datacenter leases at Q3 FY26), the principal vector by which the buildout is actually financed. aggregate_datacenter_purchase_commitments_usd is total compute/datacenter commitments (an UPPER BOUND on what flows to the financed core; the filings rarely name the neocloud recipient). Capex mixes AI-specific and total where AI is not separately disclosed.

So at the contract level the downside lands on PARENT EQUITY, not ring-fenced into the SPVs -- a creditor of the facility can reach the parent, so equity holders (not just facility lenders) eat the loss. contract_structure.note: Contract-level who-bears-downside, from the actual credit-agreement / guaranty exhibits (adversarially verified; non-recourse / bankruptcy-remote claims rejected unless the document states them, so those counts are conservative). full_recourse_to_parent / parent-guaranteed facilities put the loss on PARENT EQUITY; non_recourse + bankruptcy-remote SPVs ring-fence it to facility creditors + pledged collateral (often GPUs). This sharpens the census-level recourse split with document-level structure.

universe_extrapolation.note: Capture-recapture (Chapman) estimate of the true AI-infra entity universe from overlapping acquisition sources -- a principled population estimate, NOT an assumed observability fraction. CAPPED at INFERRED tier (<=0.45); near-disjoint source pairs are flagged + excluded (independence violated). The forward band is a labeled SENSITIVITY, not a forecast. Load-bearing use is the distress-robustness check (distress stays ~4% at any plausible true size), not the point estimate. Never drives the verdict or the evidence gate.

gpu_earnings_quality.earnings_quality_read: earnings_overstated_by_understated_depreciation (UPPER BOUND): restating depreciation at a ~3yr economic life adds ~$2.95B/yr across 6 issuers that disclose the inputs. This is an UPPER BOUND, not a point estimate: the method scales each issuer's ENTIRE D&A by the life ratio, but D&A also covers genuinely long-lived assets (data-center shells, electrical, leasehold up to ~12yr) that should NOT be re-lived at 3yr -- a compute-gross-weighted restatement is materially lower (e.g. CoreWeave ~$1.6B vs ~$2.45B here). The DIRECTION is robust (every restated issuer worsens; CoreWeave's loss roughly triples), but read the figure as a ceiling. Caveat Nebius: it is already operationally loss-making (continuing-ops NI ~+$10M; its positive headline NI is discontinued-ops + equity-revaluation gains), so the restatement deepens, not creates, its loss.
gpu_earnings_quality.note: GPU depreciation earnings-quality. Compute PP&E, accounting useful life, and D&A are primary-sourced per issuer; the 3.0yr economic life is a labeled ASSUMPTION (defensible from rental-yield compression). 'Understatement' = restated depreciation at economic life minus accounting depreciation on the same net book value -- the amount by which D&A is understated and pre-tax earnings overstated each year. TAM realism = realized AI/cloud revenue as a % of the cited TAM (tiny capture = aspirational). Only filing-verified inputs contribute; nothing invented.

dimensions.question: Does the debt mature AFTER the GPU collateral is economically dead?
dimensions.measured: peak debt horizon ~48mo vs ~24mo GPU economic life
dimensions.interpretation: Met: the collateral is economically worthless ~24mo before the debt matures, so a secured lender cannot be made whole on the GPUs -- the defining structural mismatch.

dimensions.question: Does the loss ring-fence to SPV creditors, or reach parent equity?
dimensions.interpretation: No principled cutoff. The structural fact: the debt is MOSTLY parent-recourse, so the loss is absorbed by parent EQUITY, not ring-fenced into an SPV-illiquidity cascade. This CONTRADICTS the framework's pessimistic guess and is itself the finding -- the channel is equity wipeout, not SPV fire-sale contagion.

dimensions.question: Is any issuer's single-customer dependence at an EXISTENTIAL (>50%) level?
dimensions.measured: 100.0% of issuers carry >35% single-customer concentration; max disclosed ~67.0% (CoreWeave/Microsoft)
dimensions.interpretation: Existential concentration present: at least one issuer derives the MAJORITY of revenue from one customer (CoreWeave ~67% Microsoft) -- losing that customer removes most revenue against fixed debt service.

dimensions.question: Does the MAJORITY of announced capacity show no physical construction?
dimensions.measured: 53.4% of 762 satellite-observed sites show NO change
dimensions.interpretation: 53.4% of observed sites show no inter-period change on Sentinel-2. This is a CONFOUNDED proxy, NOT proof of un-built capacity: 'no change' includes sites that are already built/operational (nothing left to change) as well as never-started ones, and carries cloud/seasonal noise. Read as a flag to pair with the construction-status proxy and permit/queue evidence -- it does not by itself meet a >50%-un-built tipping line, so it is reported as magnitude, not a satisfied condition.

dimensions.question: Is the leveraged tail large enough to be a SYSTEMIC (vs contained) risk?
dimensions.measured: 4.3% of 649 classified AI-infra entities are financed_ai_infra_leveraged
dimensions.interpretation: No principled cutoff for 'systemic'. The magnitude: the leveraged tail is a SMALL share of the classified AI-infra universe, and the broad debt metric is dominated by non-AI debt -- so the loss is CONTAINED to a small, specific cluster rather than an ecosystem-wide tail. This contradicts the framework's pessimistic guess and reinforces the scoped (not ecosystem-wide) verdict.

fragility_scorecard.composite_read: first_principles_tipping_conditions_met: 2 of the defensible economic tipping conditions are SATISFIED by the data (asset_liability_duration_mismatch, customer_concentration) -- collateral dies before the debt matures, and a single customer sits at an existential (>50%) share of revenue. The execution/satellite leg is a CONFOUNDED proxy (satellite 'no-change' conflates un-built with already-built), so it is reported as magnitude and NOT counted as a met condition. The two dimensions without a principled binary (recourse, leveraged-tail size) show the loss is borne by parent EQUITY and confined to a SMALL share of the universe -- so the failure mode is severe distress WITHIN a bounded cluster, not an ecosystem-wide cascade. No borrowed threshold was trusted; each line is first-principles or the raw magnitude.
fragility_scorecard.note: Forensic fragility: the dimensions (questions) are inspired by an external framework, but its numeric thresholds are NOT adopted -- they are unvalidated guesses. A tipping line is applied ONLY where a first-principles economic condition is defensible AND cleanly measured (duration: debt > asset life; concentration: single customer > 50% of revenue). The execution/satellite leg is reported as MAGNITUDE only -- its 'no-change' signal conflates un-built with already-built sites, so it is not a clean tipping condition. Recourse and tail-size have no principled binary, so the structural fact and magnitude are reported instead -- and on both, the data CONTRADICTS the framework's pessimistic guesses (mostly parent-recourse; small leveraged tail), which is the honest finding.

risks.evidence: Cluster EBITDA/interest ~1.35x but 7/11 issuers loss-making; ex-CoreWeave aggregate EBITDA negative. Forward stress: 8 issuers breach by the ADVERSE case (25% util miss + 200bp).

risks.title: Refinancing treadmill on negative carry
risks.evidence: Cluster debt $54.8B; maturities spread 2026-2034 (~28.6% near-term 2025-2027, ~40.4% 2030-2033) refinanced at 6-10% / SOFR+225-400bp.

risks.title: Anchor-customer concentration: a single pullback collapses contracted revenue
risks.evidence: customer_concentration_over_35pct present in 8/8 issuers (e.g. CoreWeave ~67% Microsoft).

risks.title: Pervasive internal-control / accounting red flags across the cluster
risks.evidence: 8/8 issuers carry a filing-tied SERIOUS flag; material_weakness_icfr present 8/8, auditor change 5, related-party/circular 7.

risks.title: Single-counterparty contagion + vendor round-trip: NVIDIA is supplier AND equity investor
risks.evidence: Shared hubs touch multiple issuers simultaneously: U.S. Bank, Wilmington Trust, NVIDIA. NVIDIA is both GPU supplier and equity investor (filing-verified circular relationship). Round-trip quantified: NVIDIA is a filing-verified equity investor in 3 of its own GPU-cloud customers (Applied Digital, CoreWeave, Nebius), 2 with a filing-verified return-purchase leg (~$4.0B reciprocal). ai_direct_core_verdict.ecosystem_verdict_basis: Not assessable as a clean ratio. $3.62T deduped materiality metric is a broad EDGAR corpus dominated by non-AI debt (casinos, student loans, utilities, telecom, cruise lines), so the AI-linked share (~$363.0B established / $142.0B direct) is NOT a meaningful 'fraction of the AI ecosystem'. No defensible total-AI-ecosystem leverage denominator exists yet, so an ecosystem-wide bubble is neither confirmed nor refuted -- only the scoped AI-direct core is assessed. The non-bubble case also remains credible (bear confidence 0.62).
source_backed_fragility_facts: 7 of 11 AI-direct issuers are loss-making (negative EBITDA); 7 of 11 cannot cover interest expense from EBITDA.

Cluster aggregate EBITDA/interest coverage is 1.35x, but leans on CoreWeave's EBITDA; the other positive-EBITDA issuers (CleanSpark, Bitdeer Technologies Group, IREN Limited) do not offset the loss-makers, so ex-CoreWeave the cluster's aggregate EBITDA is negative.
Debt service INCLUDING principal is well below 1x where disclosed (CoreWeave ~0.30x with its 2026 principal wall): interest is covered, principal only by refinancing.

who_bears_downside_quantified.basis_caveat: Split is on disclosed FACILITY PRINCIPAL, whose sum can exceed net drawn debt because some facilities report committed size, not drawn balance -- read the PROPORTIONS, not the absolute, as the loss-bearer mix.
who_bears_downside_quantified.note: Front-line loss-bearer by disclosed facility recourse. full_recourse_secured = secured on GPU/SPV collateral AND parent/unconditionally guaranteed (downside flows to PARENT equity; GPU collateral is the creditor backstop) -- this corrects the 'bankruptcy-remote ring-fencing' read: most AI-direct debt is parent-recourse or unsecured-at-parent (the parent, i.e. equity, absorbs the bulk). non_recourse_secured = secured creditors bear it on GPU collateral only. unsecured = general creditors. Ratepayers/insurers/pensions are downstream and not in this split.

Applied Digital -> NVIDIA -> OpenAI -> CoreWeave -> Applied Digital

circular_financing.disclosure_gap: Neither NVIDIA's nor Microsoft's filings name the supplier-AND-investor circularity (NVIDIA) or the Microsoft->OpenAI->CoreWeave->NVIDIA chain as a related-party or customer/supplier-concentration risk; NVIDIA's customer concentration is anonymized (Customer A/B/C). The round-trip is forensic framing, not a filing-disclosed risk -- a disclosure-gap red flag in its own right.
circular_financing.demand_durability_read: NVIDIA is a filing-verified equity investor in 3 of its own GPU-cloud customers (Applied Digital, CoreWeave, Nebius); 2 have a filing-verified return-purchase leg, closing ~$4.0B of reciprocal (supplier-funds-customer) capital. 2 reciprocal loop(s) are filing-verified on every leg CoreWeave -> NVIDIA -> CoreWeave; NVIDIA -> Nebius -> NVIDIA. 4 larger macro loop(s) exist but rest on a press-reported/inferred edge (e.g. the NVIDIA->OpenAI framework commitment), so they are flagged and capped, not relied on. Net: the AI-infra demand signal is partly reciprocal -- the supplier finances the buyers -- so headline take-or-pay backlog overstates independent, arm's-length end-demand.
circular_financing.interpretation_caveat: The equity-investment and GPU-purchase legs are LEGALLY SEPARATE transactions; their co-existence does not prove the identical dollars circulate (Nebius is the one filing that earmarks the supplier's proceeds for the supplier's hardware). The defensible inference is narrower and still material: the dominant supplier is also an equity investor in its own customers, so (a) it is incentivized to sustain their apparent demand and (b) the demand those customers represent is NOT arm's-length -- a vendor-financed buyer is not an independent validator of end-demand. This impairs demand DURABILITY; it is a red flag, not proof of fabricated revenue.
circular_financing.note: Reciprocal/round-trip financing detection via directed money-flow cycle search. Filing-verified loops are primary-source on every leg; loops touching a press-reported or inferred edge are FLAGGED and capped at INFERRED (<=0.45) -- they never drive the verdict. Vendor round-tripping is the Lucent/Nortel late-cycle tell; the finding here is that the structure is present and partly filing-verified, which is itself novel relative to the purely customer-concentration framing.

per_offtaker.basis: Pre-profitability. Microsoft carries OpenAI under the equity method (HLBV) as a 'funding commitment' with revenue-sharing and recognized large OpenAI-related equity-method swings; OpenAI is capitalized by Microsoft ($13B), an NVIDIA letter of intent (up to $100B, NON-BINDING, $0 funded), and SoftBank. Its ~$18.4B multi-year CoreWeave take-or-pay far exceeds its operating cash flow and depends on continued external fundraising -- it cannot be honored from operations. Fragile demand, and circular (its compute vendor's supplier and its largest backer are inside the same loop).

Hyperscaler with large positive operating cash flow; the ~$14.2B commitment is spread through December 2031 (~$2.4B/yr), small vs annual operating cash flow and payable from operations. Durable demand. (Funding-class is a first-principles judgment; no single offtaker-cash-flow figure is cited here.)

fragile_demand_failure_cascade.trigger_basis: Seeded from the capital-markets-dependent offtaker(s) the durability layer flags as most likely to fail. The 'debt_at_risk_usd' is the directly-hit issuer's ENTIRE total debt (e.g. CoreWeave's full ~$25B), NOT apportioned to this offtaker's revenue share -- it is a gross UPPER BOUND on directly-exposed leverage, not a probability-weighted or offtaker-attributable loss. The fragile offtaker is one of several customers (Microsoft is CoreWeave's largest at ~67%), so its withdrawal alone would impair, not necessarily zero, the issuer; read this as 'the leverage sitting on the issuer the fragile demand touches', a contagion-surface measure.

demand_funding_durability.durability_read: 56.4% of the cluster's CLASSIFIED named take-or-pay backlog (~$18.4B of $32.6B) rests on capital_markets_dependent offtaker(s) (OpenAI) -- demand that is NOT payable from the offtaker's operations and depends on continued external fundraising. A MAJORITY of the named contracted demand is therefore a bet on open capital markets, not on end-customer operating cash flow -- and (via the circular-financing loop) that offtaker is partly funded by the cluster's own GPU supplier and largest current customer. The hyperscaler slices remain durable; the contracted-backlog 'proof of demand' is bifurcated, and its larger half is the fragile, circular one.
demand_funding_durability.caveat: Dollar commitments are filing-verified; the funding-class is a FIRST-PRINCIPLES judgment (payable-from-operations vs requires-external-capital) backed by the cited filing where one exists. The hyperscaler slices (Microsoft, Meta) are genuinely durable -- the finding is the BIFURCATION of demand, not blanket fragility. SCOPE: the percentage is of the NAMED, classified backlog only (OpenAI + Meta dollar commitments); Microsoft's commitment is sized only as ~67% of CoreWeave revenue (no multi-year dollar figure disclosed) and is durable, so the fragile share of TOTAL contracted demand is LOWER than the named-slice figure -- the precise claim is 'a majority of the NAMED take-or-pay backlog', not of all demand. Capped as a corroborating decomposition; never drives the evidence gate.

demand_side_funding.bear_case_read: mixed_and_weakening: aggregate operating cash flow still covers AI cash capex (1.76x) and the largest players (Microsoft/Meta) self-fund, BUT the demand side is NOT uniformly cash-funded -- 2 player(s) are predominantly debt-funded (e.g. Oracle, capex > OCF), others use mixed debt, and the mega-caps carry large OFF-BALANCE-SHEET datacenter lease pipelines NOT in this ratio. So the bear/rational-growth case holds for the cash-rich core of the demand side today, but leverage is rising at the margin and via off-BS leases -- the demand side is not an unconditional backstop for the financed core.

power_ratepayer_exposure.ratepayer_downside_read: ratepayers_largely_protected: AI-datacenter power cost is mostly borne by the customer via special tariffs / minimum-take with collateral, limiting ratepayer stranded-asset exposure. Verify the min-take actually survives a customer pullback (carve-outs).

example_household_routed_holders: Vanguard Group, Inc. (filer: Vanguard Portfolio Management LLC)
ultimate_end_holders.ultimate_downside_read: mixed_holding: disclosed holders span household-routed (insurance/pension/index) and risk-capital, with no majority either way; the undisclosed private-placement debt is the swing factor for where the ultimate loss concentrates.
ultimate_end_holders.coverage_caveat: Disclosed-holder distribution from SEC ownership filings (13F-HR, SC 13G/13D, S-1/10-K beneficial ownership); equity-heavy. Most DDTL/SPV debt is a private placement with NO 13-F, so undisclosed debt holders are not in this equity mix; the debt-side routing is resolved separately in debt_side_funding_routing.

debt_side_funding_routing.debt_side_downside_read: debt_side_routes_to_households: 8 of 8 cluster lenders draw a material share of their credit capital from INSURANCE/ANNUITY balance sheets or PENSIONS (median ~41.0% of credit capital insurance-funded among lenders that disclose it). So the cluster's private-placement DEBT loss -- invisible in 13-F equity data -- routes to policyholders and retirees, the same quiet, socialized channel as 2008. This is the resolved debt-side complement to the equity end-holder mix and a hidden, under-discussed downside concentration.
debt_side_funding_routing.caveat: Lenders' AGGREGATE funding mix (insurance/annuity + pension share of credit capital) from their own filings -- NOT a per-DDTL-facility attribution to the cluster's specific debt, which is undisclosed.

supply_side_equipment_constraints.constraint_read: binding_equipment_chokepoints: 8 chokepoint(s) are both hard/material AND gate the buildout with lead times up to ~42 months -- a physical cap on how fast announced AI capacity can convert to revenue, independent of demand or financing. Of these, Backup gensets / reciprocating engines, Gas turbines, HBM memory, Large power transformers & switchgear, Liquid cooling / thermal, TSMC CoWoS advanced packaging is/are SINGLE-SOURCE or duopoly -- a shock there propagates across every downstream issuer simultaneously (the supply-side analogue of the NVIDIA hub), and a leading indicator the market under-weights versus headline demand.

issuers_with_serious_accounting_flag: Cipher Mining Inc. / Cipher Digital Inc.
forensic_red_flags.red_flag_read: serious_accounting_flags_present: 8 of 8 issuers carry a filing-tied SERIOUS flag (going-concern / material weakness / restatement / auditor exit): Applied Digital Corporation, Cipher Mining Inc. / Cipher Digital Inc., Core Scientific, CoreWeave, Hut 8 Corp., IREN Limited, Nebius Group N.V., TeraWulf Inc.. These are the highest-conviction forensic tells and concentrate where a distress event is most likely to surface first.
forensic_red_flags.note: Filing-verified forensic red-flag checklist per issuer (severity-weighted; only PRESENT, source-tied flags score; serious accounting flags rejected if unsourced). Absence of a serious flag is not a clean bill -- only that none was disclosed in the window read.

cluster_boundary_test.boundary_read: cluster_is_bounded: only 1 of 6 adjacent candidate names qualify as genuine financed AI-infra (Bit Digital); 5 are crypto-only-with-marginal-AI and 0 not relevant. The financed-AI buildout does NOT balloon when you probe adjacent names -- it is a small, specific, leveraged set. This reinforces the scoped verdict: bubble dynamics in a bounded financed cluster, not an ecosystem-wide phenomenon.

contract_level_recourse.who_bears_downside_read: loss_concentrates_on_parent_equity: of 22 contract-verified facilities, 16 are full-recourse-to-parent and 8 are parent-guaranteed vs 2 non-recourse (1 bankruptcy-remote). So at the contract level the downside lands on PARENT EQUITY, not ring-fenced into the SPVs -- a creditor of the facility can reach the parent, so equity holders (not just facility lenders) eat the loss. This corroborates the census-level recourse finding with document language.

weakest_links_ranked.ranking_read: weakest_link_is_Core_Scientific: highest composite risk (19.0) driven by restatement (present), material_weakness_icfr (present), customer_concentration_over_35pct (present). 8/8 entities carry a serious accounting flag and 5/8 are EBITDA-negative -- the fragility is broad across the cluster, not concentrated in one name, so an idiosyncratic distress event would land in a correlated set.

utilization_debt_service_mismatch.mismatch_read: revenue_below_debt_service: 1 of 1 issuers that filed full debt service have REVENUE below it (coverage < 1x): Cipher Mining Inc. / Cipher Digital Inc.. Even total revenue does not cover principal+interest -- a hard, disclosed mismatch, not a utilization-miss tail. Note: per-deal utilization and full debt service are rarely cleanly filed, so the computable sample is thin; the absence of a ratio for an issuer is non-disclosure, not safety.

risks.title: Cluster cash-flow fragility: positive coverage leans on one issuer and flips negative under a moderate shock
risks.evidence: Cluster EBITDA/interest ~1.35x but 7/11 issuers loss-making; ex-CoreWeave aggregate EBITDA negative. Forward stress: 8 issuers breach by the ADVERSE case (25% util miss + 200bp).

risks.title: Refinancing treadmill on negative carry
risks.evidence: Cluster debt $54.8B; maturities spread 2026-2034 (~28.6% near-term 2025-2027, ~40.4% 2030-2033) refinanced at 6-10% / SOFR+225-400bp.

risks.title: Anchor-customer concentration: a single pullback collapses contracted revenue
risks.evidence: customer_concentration_over_35pct present in 8/8 issuers (e.g. CoreWeave ~67% Microsoft).

risks.title: Pervasive internal-control / accounting red flags across the cluster
risks.evidence: 8/8 issuers carry a filing-tied SERIOUS flag; material_weakness_icfr present 8/8, auditor change 5, related-party/circular 7.

risks.title: Single-counterparty contagion + vendor round-trip: NVIDIA is supplier AND equity investor
risks.evidence: Shared hubs touch multiple issuers simultaneously: U.S. Bank, Wilmington Trust, NVIDIA. NVIDIA is both GPU supplier and equity investor (filing-verified circular relationship). Round-trip quantified: NVIDIA is a filing-verified equity investor in 3 of its own GPU-cloud customers (Applied Digital, CoreWeave, Nebius), 2 with a filing-verified return-purchase leg (~$4.0B reciprocal). Vendor-financed demand is not arm's-length -- the Lucent/Nortel late-cycle tell.

risks.title: GPU economic life shorter than the depreciation schedule
risks.evidence: Deployed-fleet rental yields down ~60-75% in ~2yr + Amazon's SEC 6->5yr server-life revision; book useful lives (5-6yr+) likely overstate recoverable value, understating depreciation/impairment.

risks.title: Earnings overstated by slow GPU depreciation: honest economic-life depreciation deepens the losses
risks.evidence: Restating GPU depreciation at ~3yr economic life adds ~$2.9B/yr of D&A across 6 issuers; 6 see earnings worsen (CoreWeave's loss ~triples; Nebius flips negative). Several EXTENDED useful lives (earnings-flattering). Inputs primary-sourced; economic life a labeled assumption.

risks.title: Physical overbuild gap: most announced AI data-center sites show no ground construction on satellite
risks.evidence: Sentinel-2 change detection over 762 georeferenced AI sites: only 14.4% show active construction; 407 show NO significant ground change -- announced capacity outrunning physical reality (read with the tracker construction-status proxy; cloud/seasonal noise applies).

risks.title: Single-source supply gate (TSMC CoWoS) caps the buildout and propagates a shock to all issuers
risks.evidence: 8/8 chokepoints gate the buildout (lead times up to ~42.0 months); CoWoS near-single-source.

risks.title: Demand-side off-balance-sheet leverage understates hyperscaler commitment risk
risks.evidence: Aggregate cash-coverage 1.76x but read 'mixed_and_weakening: aggregate operating cash flow still covers AI cash capex (1.76x) and the largest players (Microsoft/Meta) self-fund, BUT the demand side is NOT uniformly cash-funded -- 2 player(s) are predominantly debt-funded (e.g. Oracle, capex > OCF), others use mixed debt, and the mega-caps carry large OFF-BALANCE-SHEET datacenter lease pipelines NOT in this ratio. So the bear/rational-growth case holds for the cash-rich core of the demand side today, but leverage is rising at the margin and via off-BS leases -- the demand side is not an unconditional backstop for the financed core.' — Oracle debt-funded + large off-BS lease pipelines outside the headline number.

risks.title: Ultimate downside socialized: cluster debt routes to insurance/pension capital (households)
risks.evidence: 8/8 private-credit lenders draw material insurance/pension funding (median ~41.0% insurance-funded) — debt-side loss lands on policyholders/retirees, invisible in 13-F equity data.

risks.title: Ratepayer stranded-asset exposure on AI grid build (largely, not fully, protected)
risks.evidence: ~$46.6B (~26.8%) of AI generation/grid build in the rate base; read 'ratepayers_largely_protected' — most cost shifted to AI customers via take-or-pay, residual on regulated utilities.

crack_timing.maturity_profile: Primary-sourced cluster maturity census (~$54.8B total debt): maturities are SPREAD 2026-2034, peaking 2030 (~$10.3B). ~40.4% falls 2030-2033 and ~28.6% is near-term 2025-2027 -- NOT an 88% cliff. The fragility is a continuous refinancing treadmill: cash-flow-negative issuers must roll debt every year, and the near-term 28.6% coincides with the timing engine's ~2026-Q2 refi-pressure peak.

forward_scenarios.severity_read: A MAJORITY of cluster issuers breach (coverage<1 or negative EBITDA) at the base scenario. The 'base' scenario applies ZERO shock (utilization miss, rate shock and GPU-life compression all nil), so the financed core is ALREADY fragile before any shock: ~7 of 11 issuers do not cover interest standalone at as-reported conditions, and the adverse/severe scenarios only deepen it. The cluster AGGREGATE still covers interest (~1.35x) ONLY because CoreWeave/CleanSpark mask the loss-makers -- ex-CoreWeave the aggregate is negative (~-0.48x).
forward_scenarios.note: Cluster cash-flow stress: base financials are primary-sourced (11-issuer fixture); the stress PARAMETERS (utilization miss, rate shock, GPU-life compression) are labeled assumptions. EBITDA falls ~1:1 with the revenue lost to a utilization miss (high fixed cost), interest reprices at refinancing by shock/avg-rate (~8%). 'Breaching' = stressed interest coverage < 1 or negative EBITDA. A MAJORITY of issuers already breach at the BASE scenario (which applies ZERO shock), so the financed core is already fragile before any shock -- the aggregate ~1.35x coverage is a CoreWeave/CleanSpark concentration artifact masking the loss-makers; the adverse/severe scenarios only deepen the breach.

Rate shock at refinancing (already SOFR+225-400bp / 6-10% fixed on negative carry).
Sustained utilization below underwriting assumptions (compresses already-thin EBITDA).
GPU rental-rate compression accelerating faster than the 5-7yr depreciation schedule.
leading_indicators: Restricted-cash / covenant-headroom erosion in DDTL facilities
RPO growth stalling or customer commitment renegotiation
Secondary GPU price / cloud rental-rate prints
New SPV/DDTL draw pace vs free cash flow

Supply-side equipment chokepoints easing or tightening (TSMC CoWoS advanced-packaging / HBM allocation, gas-turbine and transformer lead times): 8 of 8 verified chokepoints currently gate the buildout (lead times up to ~42.0 months) -- a loosening is a demand-cooling tell, a further tightening caps revenue conversion.

weakest_links: CoreWeave dominates cluster EBITDA (~$2.4B of the cluster's net) and is the only large issuer with a near-term principal wall ($6.7B due 2026; DSCR incl. principal ~0.30x); 67% of its revenue is one customer (Microsoft). Positive cluster interest coverage leans on it -- ex-CoreWeave aggregate EBITDA is negative.

7 of 11 issuers are loss-making and cannot cover interest from EBITDA; the negative ex-CoreWeave aggregate is driven by the large loss-makers (MARA, Nebius, Cipher), though CleanSpark, Bitdeer Technologies Group, IREN Limited do individually cover interest.

GPU collateral: ~5-7yr book life vs observed economic-life compression -- deployed-fleet rental yields fell ~60-75% in ~18-24 months (source-backed market data) and Amazon's SEC filing already cut server life 6->5yr. Book life overstates the secured collateral's monetization window. (Caveat: newest gen still appreciating; gap clearest on rental yield.)

bear_case.summary: The non-bubble (rational-growth) view is well-supported by this repo's own primary data, and notably the bubble engine cannot refute it. After scanning 197,243 filings, the purpose-built bear engine caps bubble confidence at 25% and concludes the final bubble call is "not yet supported": of its $3.62T deduped exposure metric only $362.98B (10.0%) has established AI/data-center linkage and just $142B (3.9%) is direct, while 90% is "not_established_linkage"; the directly AI-linked capital graph is only $4.75B and the $44.6T "contagion" figure is self-labeled inflated/not-exposure.
bear_case.key_caveat: The strongest non-bubble evidence here is partly an ABSENCE of proof rather than positive proof of health: the bear engine's cash-flow-mismatch and GPU-depreciation-compression tests are BLOCKED/uncomputed for missing source-backed inputs, so "no demonstrable bubble" partly reflects an ...

caveats: Scope: the AI-direct core is a specific named cluster, not a fixed % of the metric; the broad metric includes large non-AI debt and cannot anchor an ecosystem ratio.

Crack timing now uses the primary-sourced 11-issuer debt census (cluster total debt ~$54.8B): maturities are spread 2026-2034 (~40% in 2030-2033, ~29% near-term), NOT an 88% 2030-2033 cliff -- the earlier curated-floor framing over-stated the wall.
2 of the 3 separation-test mismatch legs (realistic-utilization DSCR, GPU depreciation gap) are blocked/illustrative; the verdict rests mainly on the source-backed cluster interest-coverage leg.

Who-bears-downside is QUANTIFIED by disclosed facility recourse (see who_bears_downside_quantified): the loss concentrates on parent equity (full-recourse-secured + unsecured-at-parent), GPU collateral the backstop for the secured slice. Contagion is mapped via SHARED-COUNTERPARTY hubs (see contagion_hubs -- the common GPU supplier / anchor customers / lenders that propagate a shock across the cluster simultaneously). The financed cluster is now INJECTED into the production capital-exposure graph as source-backed deals (issuer debt -> lead arranger, plus GPU supplier / strategic investor / anchor-customer topology edges), lifting the graph's AI-infra-relevant notional from ~$5B (Equinix only) to ~$56B and surfacing the shared lenders (Goldman, Morgan Stanley) and NVIDIA/Microsoft as cross-cluster hubs in the same graph as the rest of the ecosystem; per-lender syndicate allocations remain undisclosed so each issuer's debt is attributed once to its lead arranger.

Physical deliverability is read from the tracker construction-status proxy: the ISO interconnection queues are fully ingested but are GENERATION-side, so they are a weak lens for data-center LOAD deliverability (a true firm-vs-queue rate needs load-interconnection data). executive_summary.overall_assessment: Final bubble/no-bubble conclusion is not yet supported. Current output is a source acquisition and evidence coverage report, not an investment conclusion.
executive_summary.coverage_sentence: Covered 197243 filings, 789787 source-backed normalized entities, 17227 projects, and 62952 source-backed deals. Compute economics coverage has 180 source-backed rows. Physical execution extraction has 821 distinct source-backed terms across 662 projects. Entity expansion found 2356 SEC CIK matches from 1397581 source-backed mentions. Acquisition catalog currently queues 586 source targets; 66660/66660 attempted artifacts are acquired. The LLM adjudication queue currently has 6773 source-backed blocker items. The materiality-first pass has packaged 6663 top blockers for automated LLM adjudication. The automated adjudication decision pass has source-quote-backed 6463 and row-context-backed 200 packet decisions and currently approves 2705 rows for metric use across 1326 deduped metric groups, with 2413 rows still requiring deeper extraction. Within the deduped final materiality metric, $0.363T has established direct/watchlist AI-data-center linkage while 90.0% does not yet have established thesis linkage. The timing calendar currently has 3263 source-backed crack-window signals. The debt-service pass has measured $16,746,362,791 of annual interest/debt-service proxy from explicit source-backed rates, with $689,881,283,166 of debt-like notional still missing explicit rate evidence.

is_this_a_bubble.answer: Tiered. ECOSYSTEM-WIDE: not assessable as a clean ratio -- the broad materiality metric is dominated by non-AI debt, so the AI-linked share is not a meaningful denominator and no defensible total-AI-leverage figure exists yet; the broad binary stays gated. AI-DIRECT CORE: bubble_dynamics_present at confidence 0.67 -- source-backed cash-flow fragility (7 of 11 issuers loss-making, refinancing-dependent, GPU-collateralized, holed take-or-pay) in the financed cluster, resting mainly on the one source-backed interest-coverage leg. See 'ai_direct_core_verdict' for the scoped verdict, reconciled crack timing, weakest links, data gaps, and bear case.

confidence_derivation.note: Source-backed cash-flow fragility is high-confidence; the bubble framing is discounted by the credible non-bubble case and forward-assumption dependence. Not a near-certainty call.

source_backed_legs: gpu_depreciation_gap (deployed-fleet rental-yield compression + Amazon's SEC 6->5yr server-life revision)
evidence_basis.note: The core verdict rests on 2 source-backed leg(s): cluster EBITDA/interest coverage and the GPU book-vs-economic-life gap (rental-yield compression + the SEC-filed Amazon useful-life revision). The realistic-utilization-DSCR leg remains illustrative pending per-deal debt-service/utilization inputs; it is NOT yet counted as proof. A second, INDEPENDENT demand-durability leg corroborates: 56.4% of the cluster's named take-or-pay backlog rests on a capital-markets-dependent, circular offtaker (OpenAI -- partly funded by the cluster's own GPU supplier and largest current customer), so the bull case's strongest evidence (the contracted backlog) is bifurcated and its larger half is not arm's-length end-demand. A first-principles judgment on filing-verified commitments, not a measured ratio -- but it attacks the demand side the cash-flow legs cannot.
corroborating_source_backed_layers: forensic red-flag scorecard (filing-verified serious accounting flags)
contract-level recourse (who bears the loss, from credit agreements)
forward cash-flow stress (majority breach by the adverse case)
demand-funding durability (majority of named backlog rests on a capital-markets-funded offtaker)
cluster-boundary test (the financed cluster is bounded)
GDS graph topology (energy/power intermediaries are the structural chokepoints; modularity weakly corroborates boundedness)

ai_direct_core_verdict.ecosystem_verdict_basis: Not assessable as a clean ratio. $3.62T deduped materiality metric is a broad EDGAR corpus dominated by non-AI debt (casinos, student loans, utilities, telecom, cruise lines), so the AI-linked share (~$363.0B established / $142.0B direct) is NOT a meaningful 'fraction of the AI ecosystem'. No defensible total-AI-ecosystem leverage denominator exists yet, so an ecosystem-wide bubble is neither confirmed nor refuted -- only the scoped AI-direct core is assessed. The non-bubble case also remains credible (bear confidence 0.62).
source_backed_fragility_facts: 7 of 11 AI-direct issuers are loss-making (negative EBITDA); 7 of 11 cannot cover interest expense from EBITDA.

Cluster aggregate EBITDA/interest coverage is 1.35x, but leans on CoreWeave's EBITDA; the other positive-EBITDA issuers (CleanSpark, Bitdeer Technologies Group, IREN Limited) do not offset the loss-makers, so ex-CoreWeave the cluster's aggregate EBITDA is negative.
Debt service INCLUDING principal is well below 1x where disclosed (CoreWeave ~0.30x with its 2026 principal wall): interest is covered, principal only by refinancing.

who_bears_downside_quantified.basis_caveat: Split is on disclosed FACILITY PRINCIPAL, whose sum can exceed net drawn debt because some facilities report committed size, not drawn balance -- read the PROPORTIONS, not the absolute, as the loss-bearer mix.
who_bears_downside_quantified.note: Front-line loss-bearer by disclosed facility recourse. full_recourse_secured = secured on GPU/SPV collateral AND parent/unconditionally guaranteed (downside flows to PARENT equity; GPU collateral is the creditor backstop) -- this corrects the 'bankruptcy-remote ring-fencing' read: most AI-direct debt is parent-recourse or unsecured-at-parent (the parent, i.e. equity, absorbs the bulk). non_recourse_secured = secured creditors bear it on GPU collateral only. unsecured = general creditors. Ratepayers/insurers/pensions are downstream and not in this split.

contagion_hubs.note: Contagion hubs = counterparties shared across >=2 AI-direct issuers. A shock to a high-issuer-count hub (e.g. the common GPU supplier, an anchor customer, a shared lender) propagates across the cluster simultaneously -- the single-points-of-failure that make idiosyncratic issuer risk systemic for the financed AI-direct core.

Applied Digital -> NVIDIA -> OpenAI -> CoreWeave -> Applied Digital

circular_financing.disclosure_gap: Neither NVIDIA's nor Microsoft's filings name the supplier-AND-investor circularity (NVIDIA) or the Microsoft->OpenAI->CoreWeave->NVIDIA chain as a related-party or customer/supplier-concentration risk; NVIDIA's customer concentration is anonymized (Customer A/B/C). The round-trip is forensic framing, not a filing-disclosed risk -- a disclosure-gap red flag in its own right.
circular_financing.demand_durability_read: NVIDIA is a filing-verified equity investor in 3 of its own GPU-cloud customers (Applied Digital, CoreWeave, Nebius); 2 have a filing-verified return-purchase leg, closing ~$4.0B of reciprocal (supplier-funds-customer) capital. 2 reciprocal loop(s) are filing-verified on every leg CoreWeave -> NVIDIA -> CoreWeave; NVIDIA -> Nebius -> NVIDIA. 4 larger macro loop(s) exist but rest on a press-reported/inferred edge (e.g. the NVIDIA->OpenAI framework commitment), so they are flagged and capped, not relied on. Net: the AI-infra demand signal is partly reciprocal -- the supplier finances the buyers -- so headline take-or-pay backlog overstates independent, arm's-length end-demand.
circular_financing.interpretation_caveat: The equity-investment and GPU-purchase legs are LEGALLY SEPARATE transactions; their co-existence does not prove the identical dollars circulate (Nebius is the one filing that earmarks the supplier's proceeds for the supplier's hardware). The defensible inference is narrower and still material: the dominant supplier is also an equity investor in its own customers, so (a) it is incentivized to sustain their apparent demand and (b) the demand those customers represent is NOT arm's-length -- a vendor-financed buyer is not an independent validator of end-demand. This impairs demand DURABILITY; it is a red flag, not proof of fabricated revenue.
circular_financing.note: Reciprocal/round-trip financing detection via directed money-flow cycle search. Filing-verified loops are primary-source on every leg; loops touching a press-reported or inferred edge are FLAGGED and capped at INFERRED (<=0.45) -- they never drive the verdict. Vendor round-tripping is the Lucent/Nortel late-cycle tell; the finding here is that the structure is present and partly filing-verified, which is itself novel relative to the purely customer-concentration framing.

per_offtaker.basis: Pre-profitability. Microsoft carries OpenAI under the equity method (HLBV) as a 'funding commitment' with revenue-sharing and recognized large OpenAI-related equity-method swings; OpenAI is capitalized by Microsoft ($13B), an NVIDIA letter of intent (up to $100B, NON-BINDING, $0 funded), and SoftBank. Its ~$18.4B multi-year CoreWeave take-or-pay far exceeds its operating cash flow and depends on continued external fundraising -- it cannot be honored from operations. Fragile demand, and circular (its compute vendor's supplier and its largest backer are inside the same loop).

Hyperscaler with large positive operating cash flow; the ~$14.2B commitment is spread through December 2031 (~$2.4B/yr), small vs annual operating cash flow and payable from operations. Durable demand. (Funding-class is a first-principles judgment; no single offtaker-cash-flow figure is cited here.)

fragile_demand_failure_cascade.trigger_basis: Seeded from the capital-markets-dependent offtaker(s) the durability layer flags as most likely to fail. The 'debt_at_risk_usd' is the directly-hit issuer's ENTIRE total debt (e.g. CoreWeave's full ~$25B), NOT apportioned to this offtaker's revenue share -- it is a gross UPPER BOUND on directly-exposed leverage, not a probability-weighted or offtaker-attributable loss. The fragile offtaker is one of several customers (Microsoft is CoreWeave's largest at ~67%), so its withdrawal alone would impair, not necessarily zero, the issuer; read this as 'the leverage sitting on the issuer the fragile demand touches', a contagion-surface measure.

demand_funding_durability.durability_read: 56.4% of the cluster's CLASSIFIED named take-or-pay backlog (~$18.4B of $32.6B) rests on capital_markets_dependent offtaker(s) (OpenAI) -- demand that is NOT payable from the offtaker's operations and depends on continued external fundraising. A MAJORITY of the named contracted demand is therefore a bet on open capital markets, not on end-customer operating cash flow -- and (via the circular-financing loop) that offtaker is partly funded by the cluster's own GPU supplier and largest current customer. The hyperscaler slices remain durable; the contracted-backlog 'proof of demand' is bifurcated, and its larger half is the fragile, circular one.
demand_funding_durability.caveat: Dollar commitments are filing-verified; the funding-class is a FIRST-PRINCIPLES judgment (payable-from-operations vs requires-external-capital) backed by the cited filing where one exists. The hyperscaler slices (Microsoft, Meta) are genuinely durable -- the finding is the BIFURCATION of demand, not blanket fragility. SCOPE: the percentage is of the NAMED, classified backlog only (OpenAI + Meta dollar commitments); Microsoft's commitment is sized only as ~67% of CoreWeave revenue (no multi-year dollar figure disclosed) and is durable, so the fragile share of TOTAL contracted demand is LOWER than the named-slice figure -- the precise claim is 'a majority of the NAMED take-or-pay backlog', not of all demand. Capped as a corroborating decomposition; never drives the evidence gate.

demand_side_funding.bear_case_read: mixed_and_weakening: aggregate operating cash flow still covers AI cash capex (1.76x) and the largest players (Microsoft/Meta) self-fund, BUT the demand side is NOT uniformly cash-funded -- 2 player(s) are predominantly debt-funded (e.g. Oracle, capex > OCF), others use mixed debt, and the mega-caps carry large OFF-BALANCE-SHEET datacenter lease pipelines NOT in this ratio. So the bear/rational-growth case holds for the cash-rich core of the demand side today, but leverage is rising at the margin and via off-BS leases -- the demand side is not an unconditional backstop for the financed core.

power_ratepayer_exposure.ratepayer_downside_read: ratepayers_largely_protected: AI-datacenter power cost is mostly borne by the customer via special tariffs / minimum-take with collateral, limiting ratepayer stranded-asset exposure. Verify the min-take actually survives a customer pullback (carve-outs).

example_household_routed_holders: Vanguard Group, Inc. (filer: Vanguard Portfolio Management LLC)
ultimate_end_holders.ultimate_downside_read: mixed_holding: disclosed holders span household-routed (insurance/pension/index) and risk-capital, with no majority either way; the undisclosed private-placement debt is the swing factor for where the ultimate loss concentrates.
ultimate_end_holders.coverage_caveat: Disclosed-holder distribution from SEC ownership filings (13F-HR, SC 13G/13D, S-1/10-K beneficial ownership); equity-heavy. Most DDTL/SPV debt is a private placement with NO 13-F, so undisclosed debt holders are not in this equity mix; the debt-side routing is resolved separately in debt_side_funding_routing.

debt_side_funding_routing.debt_side_downside_read: debt_side_routes_to_households: 8 of 8 cluster lenders draw a material share of their credit capital from INSURANCE/ANNUITY balance sheets or PENSIONS (median ~41.0% of credit capital insurance-funded among lenders that disclose it). So the cluster's private-placement DEBT loss -- invisible in 13-F equity data -- routes to policyholders and retirees, the same quiet, socialized channel as 2008. This is the resolved debt-side complement to the equity end-holder mix and a hidden, under-discussed downside concentration.
debt_side_funding_routing.caveat: Lenders' AGGREGATE funding mix (insurance/annuity + pension share of credit capital) from their own filings -- NOT a per-DDTL-facility attribution to the cluster's specific debt, which is undisclosed.

supply_side_equipment_constraints.constraint_read: binding_equipment_chokepoints: 8 chokepoint(s) are both hard/material AND gate the buildout with lead times up to ~42 months -- a physical cap on how fast announced AI capacity can convert to revenue, independent of demand or financing. Of these, Backup gensets / reciprocating engines, Gas turbines, HBM memory, Large power transformers & switchgear, Liquid cooling / thermal, TSMC CoWoS advanced packaging is/are SINGLE-SOURCE or duopoly -- a shock there propagates across every downstream issuer simultaneously (the supply-side analogue of the NVIDIA hub), and a leading indicator the market under-weights versus headline demand.

issuers_with_serious_accounting_flag: Cipher Mining Inc. / Cipher Digital Inc.
forensic_red_flags.red_flag_read: serious_accounting_flags_present: 8 of 8 issuers carry a filing-tied SERIOUS flag (going-concern / material weakness / restatement / auditor exit): Applied Digital Corporation, Cipher Mining Inc. / Cipher Digital Inc., Core Scientific, CoreWeave, Hut 8 Corp., IREN Limited, Nebius Group N.V., TeraWulf Inc.. These are the highest-conviction forensic tells and concentrate where a distress event is most likely to surface first.
forensic_red_flags.note: Filing-verified forensic red-flag checklist per issuer (severity-weighted; only PRESENT, source-tied flags score; serious accounting flags rejected if unsourced). Absence of a serious flag is not a clean bill -- only that none was disclosed in the window read.

cluster_boundary_test.boundary_read: cluster_is_bounded: only 1 of 6 adjacent candidate names qualify as genuine financed AI-infra (Bit Digital); 5 are crypto-only-with-marginal-AI and 0 not relevant. The financed-AI buildout does NOT balloon when you probe adjacent names -- it is a small, specific, leveraged set. This reinforces the scoped verdict: bubble dynamics in a bounded financed cluster, not an ecosystem-wide phenomenon.

contract_level_recourse.who_bears_downside_read: loss_concentrates_on_parent_equity: of 22 contract-verified facilities, 16 are full-recourse-to-parent and 8 are parent-guaranteed vs 2 non-recourse (1 bankruptcy-remote). So at the contract level the downside lands on PARENT EQUITY, not ring-fenced into the SPVs -- a creditor of the facility can reach the parent, so equity holders (not just facility lenders) eat the loss. This corroborates the census-level recourse finding with document language.

weakest_links_ranked.ranking_read: weakest_link_is_Core_Scientific: highest composite risk (19.0) driven by restatement (present), material_weakness_icfr (present), customer_concentration_over_35pct (present). 8/8 entities carry a serious accounting flag and 5/8 are EBITDA-negative -- the fragility is broad across the cluster, not concentrated in one name, so an idiosyncratic distress event would land in a correlated set.

utilization_debt_service_mismatch.mismatch_read: revenue_below_debt_service: 1 of 1 issuers that filed full debt service have REVENUE below it (coverage < 1x): Cipher Mining Inc. / Cipher Digital Inc.. Even total revenue does not cover principal+interest -- a hard, disclosed mismatch, not a utilization-miss tail. Note: per-deal utilization and full debt service are rarely cleanly filed, so the computable sample is thin; the absence of a ratio for an issuer is non-disclosure, not safety.

risks.title: Cluster cash-flow fragility: positive coverage leans on one issuer and flips negative under a moderate shock
risks.evidence: Cluster EBITDA/interest ~1.35x but 7/11 issuers loss-making; ex-CoreWeave aggregate EBITDA negative. Forward stress: 8 issuers breach by the ADVERSE case (25% util miss + 200bp).

risks.title: Refinancing treadmill on negative carry
risks.evidence: Cluster debt $54.8B; maturities spread 2026-2034 (~28.6% near-term 2025-2027, ~40.4% 2030-2033) refinanced at 6-10% / SOFR+225-400bp.

risks.title: Anchor-customer concentration: a single pullback collapses contracted revenue
risks.evidence: customer_concentration_over_35pct present in 8/8 issuers (e.g. CoreWeave ~67% Microsoft).

risks.title: Pervasive internal-control / accounting red flags across the cluster
risks.evidence: 8/8 issuers carry a filing-tied SERIOUS flag; material_weakness_icfr present 8/8, auditor change 5, related-party/circular 7.

risks.title: Single-counterparty contagion + vendor round-trip: NVIDIA is supplier AND equity investor
risks.evidence: Shared hubs touch multiple issuers simultaneously: U.S. Bank, Wilmington Trust, NVIDIA. NVIDIA is both GPU supplier and equity investor (filing-verified circular relationship). Round-trip quantified: NVIDIA is a filing-verified equity investor in 3 of its own GPU-cloud customers (Applied Digital, CoreWeave, Nebius), 2 with a filing-verified return-purchase leg (~$4.0B reciprocal). Vendor-financed demand is not arm's-length -- the Lucent/Nortel late-cycle tell.

risks.title: GPU economic life shorter than the depreciation schedule
risks.evidence: Deployed-fleet rental yields down ~60-75% in ~2yr + Amazon's SEC 6->5yr server-life revision; book useful lives (5-6yr+) likely overstate recoverable value, understating depreciation/impairment.

risks.title: Earnings overstated by slow GPU depreciation: honest economic-life depreciation deepens the losses
risks.evidence: Restating GPU depreciation at ~3yr economic life adds ~$2.9B/yr of D&A across 6 issuers; 6 see earnings worsen (CoreWeave's loss ~triples; Nebius flips negative). Several EXTENDED useful lives (earnings-flattering). Inputs primary-sourced; economic life a labeled assumption.

risks.title: Physical overbuild gap: most announced AI data-center sites show no ground construction on satellite
risks.evidence: Sentinel-2 change detection over 762 georeferenced AI sites: only 14.4% show active construction; 407 show NO significant ground change -- announced capacity outrunning physical reality (read with the tracker construction-status proxy; cloud/seasonal noise applies).

risks.title: Single-source supply gate (TSMC CoWoS) caps the buildout and propagates a shock to all issuers
risks.evidence: 8/8 chokepoints gate the buildout (lead times up to ~42.0 months); CoWoS near-single-source.

risks.title: Demand-side off-balance-sheet leverage understates hyperscaler commitment risk
risks.evidence: Aggregate cash-coverage 1.76x but read 'mixed_and_weakening: aggregate operating cash flow still covers AI cash capex (1.76x) and the largest players (Microsoft/Meta) self-fund, BUT the demand side is NOT uniformly cash-funded -- 2 player(s) are predominantly debt-funded (e.g. Oracle, capex > OCF), others use mixed debt, and the mega-caps carry large OFF-BALANCE-SHEET datacenter lease pipelines NOT in this ratio. So the bear/rational-growth case holds for the cash-rich core of the demand side today, but leverage is rising at the margin and via off-BS leases -- the demand side is not an unconditional backstop for the financed core.' — Oracle debt-funded + large off-BS lease pipelines outside the headline number.

risks.title: Ultimate downside socialized: cluster debt routes to insurance/pension capital (households)
risks.evidence: 8/8 private-credit lenders draw material insurance/pension funding (median ~41.0% insurance-funded) — debt-side loss lands on policyholders/retirees, invisible in 13-F equity data.

risks.title: Ratepayer stranded-asset exposure on AI grid build (largely, not fully, protected)
risks.evidence: ~$46.6B (~26.8%) of AI generation/grid build in the rate base; read 'ratepayers_largely_protected' — most cost shifted to AI customers via take-or-pay, residual on regulated utilities.

crack_timing.maturity_profile: Primary-sourced cluster maturity census (~$54.8B total debt): maturities are SPREAD 2026-2034, peaking 2030 (~$10.3B). ~40.4% falls 2030-2033 and ~28.6% is near-term 2025-2027 -- NOT an 88% cliff. The fragility is a continuous refinancing treadmill: cash-flow-negative issuers must roll debt every year, and the near-term 28.6% coincides with the timing engine's ~2026-Q2 refi-pressure peak.

The cluster AGGREGATE still covers interest (~1.35x) ONLY because CoreWeave/CleanSpark mask the loss-makers -- ex-CoreWeave the aggregate is negative (~-0.48x).
forward_scenarios.note: Cluster cash-flow stress: base financials are primary-sourced (11-issuer fixture); the stress PARAMETERS (utilization miss, rate shock, GPU-life compression) are labeled assumptions. EBITDA falls ~1:1 with the revenue lost to a utilization miss (high fixed cost), interest reprices at refinancing by shock/avg-rate (~8%). 'Breaching' = stressed interest coverage < 1 or negative EBITDA. A MAJORITY of issuers already breach at the BASE scenario (which applies ZERO shock), so the financed core is already fragile before any shock -- the aggregate ~1.35x coverage is a CoreWeave/CleanSpark concentration artifact masking the loss-makers; the adverse/severe scenarios only deepen the breach.

earlier_triggers: A single large-customer pullback or non-performance (CoreWeave 67% Microsoft) collapses contracted-revenue coverage.
Rate shock at refinancing (already SOFR+225-400bp / 6-10% fixed on negative carry).
Sustained utilization below underwriting assumptions (compresses already-thin EBITDA).
GPU rental-rate compression accelerating faster than the 5-7yr depreciation schedule.
leading_indicators: Restricted-cash / covenant-headroom erosion in DDTL facilities
RPO growth stalling or customer commitment renegotiation
Secondary GPU price / cloud rental-rate prints
New SPV/DDTL draw pace vs free cash flow

Supply-side equipment chokepoints easing or tightening (TSMC CoWoS advanced-packaging / HBM allocation, gas-turbine and transformer lead times): 8 of 8 verified chokepoints currently gate the buildout (lead times up to ~42.0 months) -- a loosening is a demand-cooling tell, a further tightening caps revenue conversion.

weakest_links: CoreWeave dominates cluster EBITDA (~$2.4B of the cluster's net) and is the only large issuer with a near-term principal wall ($6.7B due 2026; DSCR incl. principal ~0.30x); 67% of its revenue is one customer (Microsoft). Positive cluster interest coverage leans on it -- ex-CoreWeave aggregate EBITDA is negative.

7 of 11 issuers are loss-making and cannot cover interest from EBITDA; the negative ex-CoreWeave aggregate is driven by the large loss-makers (MARA, Nebius, Cipher), though CleanSpark, Bitdeer Technologies Group, IREN Limited do individually cover interest.

GPU collateral: ~5-7yr book life vs observed economic-life compression -- deployed-fleet rental yields fell ~60-75% in ~18-24 months (source-backed market data) and Amazon's SEC filing already cut server life 6->5yr. Book life overstates the secured collateral's monetization window. (Caveat: newest gen still appreciating; gap clearest on rental yield.)

caveats: Scope: the AI-direct core is a specific named cluster, not a fixed % of the metric; the broad metric includes large non-AI debt and cannot anchor an ecosystem ratio.

Crack timing now uses the primary-sourced 11-issuer debt census (cluster total debt ~$54.8B): maturities are spread 2026-2034 (~40% in 2030-2033, ~29% near-term), NOT an 88% 2030-2033 cliff -- the earlier curated-floor framing over-stated the wall.
2 of the 3 separation-test mismatch legs (realistic-utilization DSCR, GPU depreciation gap) are blocked/illustrative; the verdict rests mainly on the source-backed cluster interest-coverage leg.

Who-bears-downside is QUANTIFIED by disclosed facility recourse (see who_bears_downside_quantified): the loss concentrates on parent equity (full-recourse-secured + unsecured-at-parent), GPU collateral the backstop for the secured slice. Contagion is mapped via SHARED-COUNTERPARTY hubs (see contagion_hubs -- the common GPU supplier / anchor customers / lenders that propagate a shock across the cluster simultaneously). The financed cluster is now INJECTED into the production capital-exposure graph as source-backed deals (issuer debt -> lead arranger, plus GPU supplier / strategic investor / anchor-customer topology edges), lifting the graph's AI-infra-relevant notional from ~$5B (Equinix only) to ~$56B and surfacing the shared lenders (Goldman, Morgan Stanley) and NVIDIA/Microsoft as cross-cluster hubs in the same graph as the rest of the ecosystem; per-lender syndicate allocations remain undisclosed so each issuer's debt is attributed once to its lead arranger.

Physical deliverability is read from the tracker construction-status proxy: the ISO interconnection queues are fully ingested but are GENERATION-side, so they are a weak lens for data-center LOAD deliverability (a true firm-vs-queue rate needs load-interconnection data). Circular-financing loop edges remain press-reported, not filing-verified.

when_cracks.answer: Partially measured, still not final. The report now computes source-backed refinancing, physical delivery, and compute-economics timing signals, but the crack window remains a candidate until the largest maturities, project COD dates, utilization evidence, power delays, and compute assumptions are LLM-adjudicated and corroborated.

indicators.measures: Whether the financed cluster's operations cover interest before any principal.
indicators.data_feed: per-issuer 10-K/10-Q EBITDA + interest expense (re-aggregate cluster census)

indicators.indicator: GPU economic life vs booked depreciation schedule
indicators.measures: Whether the collateral decays faster than it is depreciated (earnings/collateral quality).
indicators.trigger: secondary GPU rental/resale price falling faster than the booked useful life implies
indicators.data_feed: secondary GPU rental-rate and resale-price prints; issuer useful-life disclosures

indicators.indicator: Near-term (2025-2027) refinancing roll on negative carry
indicators.measures: Debt that must be rolled while the issuer is cash-flow negative, exposed to rate at roll.
indicators.stress_direction: rising refi rate / shrinking covenant headroom into the roll
indicators.trigger: refi rate at roll exceeds the asset cash yield (deepening negative carry)
indicators.data_feed: issuer maturity schedules + credit-spread / new-issue coupon prints

indicators.measures: Filing-verified loops where the dominant GPU supplier also funds the buyer (NVIDIA).
indicators.stress_direction: either way is a tell: MORE injections = demand less arm's-length; the supplier HALTING injections removes a prop the buyers may not stand without
indicators.trigger: a filing-verified reciprocal loop exists (present), or NVIDIA pauses customer funding
indicators.data_feed: NVIDIA equity-injection announcements + investee 10-K subsequent-events / PIPE filings

indicators.measures: Share of georeferenced announced sites with no visible ground construction (Sentinel-2).
indicators.stress_direction: rising stall rate (announced != real; debt service can precede energized capacity)
indicators.trigger: majority of observed sites show no construction (> 50%)
indicators.data_feed: Sentinel-2 change detection over the site list (re-run satellite_progress.py)

indicators.indicator: Supply-side equipment lead times (CoWoS/HBM, transformers, turbines)
indicators.measures: Whether the physical buildout is gated by single-source/duopoly chokepoints.
indicators.stress_direction: two-sided: loosening = demand cooling tell; tightening = revenue conversion capped
indicators.trigger: no single line -- a regime change in either direction is the signal
indicators.data_feed: supplier lead-time disclosures (TSMC/SK hynix/GE Vernova etc.); order-book commentary

indicators.measures: Whether any issuer depends on one customer for an existential share of revenue.
indicators.stress_direction: any large-customer renegotiation, pullback, or non-performance
indicators.trigger: single customer > 50% of an issuer's revenue (existential)
indicators.data_feed: issuer 10-K customer-concentration disclosure; RPO / commitment renegotiation news

leading_indicator_monitor.composite_read: 4 of 7 leading indicators are ALREADY flashing on a measured, first-principles line (not a forecast): GPU economic life vs booked depreciation schedule, Vendor round-trip dependence (supplier-as-investor), Satellite construction-stall rate, Single-customer revenue concentration (max issuer). The remaining dials are forward triggers or two-sided monitors to watch into the 2025-Q3..2027-Q3 refinancing window. The financed core is not waiting on a future catalyst to be fragile -- several stress conditions are present now; the open question is the timing of the financing/demand shock that converts present fragility into distress.
leading_indicator_monitor.note: Forward leading-indicator monitor synthesized from the source-backed layers. Each indicator names its data feed so updates are mechanical. 'currently_flashing' requires a MEASURED reading past a defensible first-principles line; forward and two-sided dials are 'watch', never flashed. This is the 'continuously update / leading indicators' capability, grounded in the same primary sources as the verdict.
